title: Guide exercise: preferred extensions, blocking
description: A starter on a fresh problem: the loop of the library example af-preferred with every refinement replaced by a block. Find the interface, write a refinement, and compare with af-preferred. See the guide page "Getting more out of each check".

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% An argumentation framework: arguments and attacks.
arg(a;b;c;d;e;f;g;h;i).
att(a,d). att(a,e). att(a,i). att(b,g). att(c,f). att(c,g). att(d,a). att(d,g).
att(e,a). att(e,g). att(e,i). att(f,c). att(g,c). att(i,e). att(i,f). att(i,h).
% Is this argument in every preferred extension?
query(a).
fragments.description: The framework and the query argument. Added to every solver.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a set of arguments that is conflict-free ...
{ in(A) } :- arg(A).
:- in(A), in(B), att(A,B).
% ... and defends its members: it attacks every attacker ...
beaten(A) :- in(B), att(B,A).
:- in(A), att(B,A), not beaten(B).
% ... and does not contain the query argument.
:- query(A), in(A).
#show in/1.
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): admissible sets without the query argument.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the members of the set.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: an admissible set that contains the candidate and one more argument
% (it may contain the query argument). Then the candidate is not maximal.
{ big(A) } :- arg(A).
:- in(A), not big(A).
:- big(A), big(B), att(A,B).
hit(A) :- big(B), att(B,A).
:- big(A), att(B,A), not hit(B).
new(A) :- big(A), not in(A).
larger :- new(A).
:- not larger.
#show big/1.

% The larger set refutes each of its proper subsets. A set survives if it has an
% argument outside the larger set, or if it contains the larger set. For each new
% argument N, clause N says: an argument outside comes in, or N comes in.
clause(N, in(A), true) :- new(N), arg(A), not big(A).
clause(N, in(N), true) :- new(N).
fragments.description: Looks for a larger admissible set (solver C) and states the refinement as clause/3 atoms.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The check states the refinement as clause(Id, Atom, Value) atoms, one clause per
# argument that the larger admissible set adds; G.block(M) reads them.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X: reject M with G.block(M)
